title: Case: Evening grocery order shows as signed for and the recipient says nobody came
context: Brineleaf Pantry order BP-928, a chilled grocery order, was booked as DL-928 for an evening slot with signature required. The recipient account and shipment match are verified.
initial_request: I watched the tracker count down to my house and then it just said delivered. Nobody in this house is called Dunmore, I don't know anyone called Dunmore. I've been through both door cameras from half six to half seven and there is no van and no person. I asked next door and they haven't got it. Brineleaf are shut till the morning and have sent me an email asking me to rate my delivery. That was tonight's dinner and most of the week for me and the two kids and they've had toast. I'm not even angry, I'm just tired. Can somebody please find out where it went.

acceptable_actions.summary: Same-day disputed handover on chilled order DL-928: signature 'R DUNMORE' on file versus the recipient's report of no visit, asking the duty investigator to review the stop tonight.

must: Gives the investigators what their notice asks for: DL-928, the signature name 'R DUNMORE' on file, and the recipient's report (no one of that name in the household, door cameras show no visit 18:30 to 19:30, neighbour does not have it).
Asks for the route stop and handover to be reviewed tonight and flags that it is a chilled grocery order.

Tells the investigators plainly that this was the household's evening meal and most of the week's food for an adult and two children, and that the merchant's support is closed until 07:00, so she has nobody else to turn to tonight.
must_not: Relies on the signature or the delivered scan as proof the order was delivered.
States or implies that the driver falsified the signature, that the order was stolen, or that it is confirmed lost or misdelivered.
Promises a redelivery tonight, a replacement, a refund or compensation.
Gives any advice on whether the food would be safe to eat if it turns up.
Sends the recipient a holding reply that tells her to wait for Brineleaf support in the morning or to check with neighbours again.
expected.reference_message: Same-day disputed handover on a chilled order, for the evening duty investigator. Shipment DL-928 (Brineleaf order BP-928), slot 18:00 to 19:00, signature required. Tracking shows delivered 18:57 UTC, signed for by 'R DUNMORE'; the signature image is on file and the stop has not been reviewed. The verified recipient, Wren Castellan, reports that nobody came to the door, nobody in her household is called Dunmore, both her door cameras show no van or person between 18:30 and 19:30, and the neighbour does not have it. Neither account is confirmed. Please review the route stop and handover record tonight and tell me what you find, with a case reference. For priority: it is chilled groceries, it was tonight's dinner and most of the week's food for her and two children, and Brineleaf support is closed until 07:00, so she has had no answer from anyone. I am not treating this as a confirmed loss and have promised her nothing.

rationale: Most of the thread is marketing, auto-replies and another shipment. The deciding facts are the signature in a name the recipient does not know, her camera and neighbour checks, and the investigators' notice that a duty investigator takes same-day chilled handover disputes until 23:00. The desk sends them that, says what the loss means to the household, and neither trusts the signature nor accuses the driver.

review.note: Coordinator emailed the duty investigator with the reference, signature name and recipient's report and ignored the noise, matching the key.
